problems.title: Read a CSV straight from the repository
problems.prompt:
This exercise shows how notebooks' data files work here.

The file `materials/datasets/sales.csv` is listed in the exercise's `data_files`, so it is copied into the sandbox and can be read with the plain file name `sales.csv`.

**Your task:** read it into a pandas DataFrame called `df`, print the DataFrame's shape, and print the total number of units sold (the sum of the `units` column).

```
df.shape      ->  (5, 3)
total units   ->  36
```
hints: `import pandas as pd` at the top.
`pd.read_csv("sales.csv")` reads the file that was placed in the working directory.
`.shape` gives (rows, columns); `.sum()` adds a column up.
Print both values — the printed order does not matter.
problems.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("sales.csv")
print(df.shape)
print(df["units"].sum())
problems.tests:
assert hasattr(df, "shape"), "df must be a pandas DataFrame"
assert df.shape == (5, 3), f"expected 5 rows and 3 columns, got {df.shape}"
assert list(df.columns) == ["product", "units", "price"], f"unexpected columns: {list(df.columns)}"
assert int(df["units"].sum()) == 36, "the units column should add up to 36"
problems.test_summary: Checks the DataFrame's shape and columns and that the units column adds up to 36.
